ai.title: Disable checkpoints for large projects
ai.summary: Checkpoints now automatically disable when project file counts exceed DEFAULT_MAX_FILES (10,000) to prevent performance degradation. The Checkpoint interface adds an enabled boolean flag, and addCheckpoint returns the full Checkpoint object instead of just the ID. CLI prompt logic was refactored to remove checkpoint number display from the main prompt, showing a success message only when checkpoints are active.

eli5.text: When you work on a very large project with more than 10,000 files, automatic save points now turn off to keep things running smoothly. You'd notice the prompt no longer shows a checkpoint number, and instead you'll only see a brief confirmation message when a save point is actually created. This only affects projects with extensive file lists; smaller projects continue saving automatically as before.

ai.title: Server-side terminal command detection replaces CLI heuristics
ai.summary: Terminal command recognition moved from client-side prefix checks and `SKIPPED_TERMINAL_COMMANDS` lists to a backend `checkTerminalCommand` function using LLM classification. The CLI no longer intercepts `!` or `/run` inputs locally; instead, the backend detects commands and triggers `run_terminal_command` with `mode: 'user'`, allowing the client to skip assistant reprompting for user-executed commands.

eli5.text: When you type what looks like a terminal command, the system now checks whether it's really a command on the remote server side using an AI classifier, instead of guessing locally with simple text matching. This means the assistant no longer needs to ask you twice to confirm that you want to run your own command, it just runs it. You would notice that commands prefixed with ! or /run, as well as plain commands the AI recognizes as terminal instructions, are executed immediately without extra back-and-forth. The client-side lists of command keywords and prefixes have been removed in favor of this centralized, smarter detection.

ai.title: Clarify request prompt tweak
ai.summary: System prompt instruction for ambiguous user commands updated in backend/src/main-prompt.ts. Trigger condition changed from general ambiguity preventing progress to explicit multiple interpretation paths, requiring at least one clarifying question instead of conditional formatting. Scope limited to core backend prompt logic; no API or CLI surface changes. Follow-up constraint: numbered list formatting instruction removed, relying on model default formatting for multi-question scenarios.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant something vague, it now asks at least one clarifying question right away instead of waiting to see if it can guess what you mean. This makes the helper more likely to respond with a straight yes/no or brief answer if that's all you need, rather than turning every exchange into a multi-part survey. You'd notice this if you gave an open-ended command and expected a list back, the numbered list now only appears when the helper actually has more than one thing to ask.

ai.title: Subgoal renderer newline logic
ai.summary: Refined `onParamEnd` in `npm-app/src/utils/tool-renderers.ts` to conditionally emit newlines. `create_subgoal` now adds newlines only for `objective` and `status`; `update_subgoal` only for `status`. This prevents excess blank lines during subgoal rendering.

eli5.text: When the assistant breaks down a task into smaller steps and shows you its progress, it stopped adding extra blank lines between some of those pieces. If you expanded one of those step summaries, the text no longer spreads out with unnecessary gaps after every detail, only after the step's goal and its current status. This only affects how those step breakdowns appear on your screen; it doesn't change what the assistant can actually do.

ai.title: Workaround for clear command in terminal
ai.summary: Added special handling for the `clear` command in `runCommandPty` within `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`. Since `node-pty` fails to clear the terminal, the code now intercepts `clear` and executes it via `execSync` with inherited stdio before spawning the PTY process.

eli5.text: When you type 'clear' in the terminal to wipe away all the text on your screen, the terminal now actually stays clean instead of keeping the old text around. The fix works by handling that one command slightly differently behind the scenes: rather than running it through the same pathway that other commands use, the system briefly uses a different method that successfully clears the display, then continues normally. You would notice this the next time you use the clear command and your screen truly empties instead of leaving faint or leftover text behind.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.176
ai.summary: Package version in npm-app/package.json updated from 1.0.175 to 1.0.176. Internal release increment. Scope limited to package manifest.

eli5.text: If you use this assistant on a very large project, it will no longer try to take automatic snapshots of your work while you're coding, which could slow things down. The way the assistant recognizes when you're asking it to run a program instead of just chat is also getting smarter, moving the decision-making behind the scenes rather than relying on a simple list of commands. You won't see a new button or setting, but you may notice the assistant is better at telling the difference between a real request and something it should ignore.

ai.title: worker-script-project-context moved to workers/project-context
ai.summary: Renamed `npm-app/src/worker-script-project-context.ts` to `npm-app/src/workers/project-context.ts`. Updated `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` to resolve the worker path from `dist/workers/project-context.js` instead of `dist/worker-script-project-context.js`. Adjusted relative imports within the worker to reference parent directory modules (`../project-files`, `../checkpoints/file-manager`).

eli5.text: The background helper that figures out which files belong to your project has been tucked into a dedicated folder, so it sits alongside other similar helpers rather than loose among general files. If you opened your project folder and looked at the source files, you'd see this helper now lives under a workers subfolder instead of being listed at the top level. The tool loads it the same way and it still does the exact same job for anyone running the project, so most people wouldn't notice anything different.

ai.title: Optimize checkpoint creation with git status checks
ai.summary: Refactored checkpoint logic in `checkpoint-manager.ts` to prevent redundant saves. Added `hasUnsavedChanges` and `getLatestCommit` helpers in `file-manager.ts` to detect clean states via `git status --porcelain` or `isomorphic-git` fallback. CLI now skips checkpoint creation if no changes exist, reducing overhead for large projects.

eli5.text: When you run a project, the tool used to save a checkpoint of your work after every single action, even if nothing in your files actually changed. Now it first checks whether your files are different from the last saved point, and only creates a checkpoint when there are real changes to record. This cuts down on extra, pointless saves, especially for big projects with lots of files, so the tool spends less time pausing to save copies of identical work. If you watch it run, you will simply see fewer checkpoint messages appear between actions, since unchanged projects no longer trigger a new save.

ai.title: Move checkpoint files to checkpoints/ directory
ai.summary: Refactors checkpoint-related modules into a dedicated `checkpoints/` directory. Updates import paths in `cli.ts`, `client.ts`, and `worker-script-project-context.ts` to reflect the new structure. Also replaces `which git` check with `git --version` in `file-manager.ts`.

eli5.text: The app's internal checkpoint-saving code was reorganized into a dedicated folder so related pieces sit together, and the files that use those pieces were updated to point at the new locations. The only visible behavior change is that the app now checks whether git is installed by running `git --version` instead of searching for git with `which git`, which makes the check more reliable on systems where `which` is not available. This is a behind-the-scenes reorganization with no effect on what you see or do in the app.

ai.title: Add princeton lite swe-bench tests to evals
ai.summary: New evals/swe-bench-ids.ts defines SWE_BENCH_IDS mapping repos to issue IDs. evals/test-repos.json adds astropy, django, flask, pytest, requests, scikit-learn, seaborn, sphinx, sympy, xarray. Internal test coverage expansion for SWE-bench lite dataset.

eli5.text: The system now runs a larger set of practice coding problems from well-known projects like Django, Flask, and scikit-learn to check how well it can solve real bug fixes. These problems come from a standard collection called the Princeton Lite SWE-bench dataset, and each one links a specific project to a known issue that developers had to fix. If you looked at the project's testing setup, you'd see a longer list of these problem IDs and new entries pointing to each project's code repositories. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping to improve the assistant's coding accuracy, and it's already active today.

ai.title: Fix SWE-bench evals
ai.summary: SWE-bench evals bug fixes. `evals/test-setup.ts` adds `master` branch fallback for git clone. `evals/swe-bench-ids.ts` and `evals/swe-bench.test.ts` updated. Internal evals surface.

eli5.text: The software now handles a situation where the usual place it looks for code to test against doesn't exist, by falling back to a common alternative location. This affects automated testing systems that verify the software works correctly against real-world bug reports and fixes from open-source projects. If you looked at the test setup configuration, you'd see it tries one git branch first, then automatically retries with a different branch name instead of failing.
